privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.lead: What we store, what we cannot see, who else is involved, and how to get your data out or deleted. Last updated October 11, 2026.
privacy.contactMail: Privacy questions, or a request about your data? Email <l1>{email}</l1>. A person reads it.

s1.t: Who we are and the short version
s1.p1: zcrypt is run by one individual, Muhammad Wasif Malik. It is not a company, and this policy does not name a registered address, representative or data protection officer because none exists. You can reach us by email at the address at the bottom of this page.
s1.p2: The short version: your files and their names are encrypted in your browser or app before they leave it, and we never receive your vault passphrase. We do store account details and metadata about your files, described below. We do not sell data, show ads or run advertising trackers.

s2.t: What we cannot see, and the limits of that
s2.l1: File contents. Encrypted on your device before upload.
s2.l2: File and folder names. Sealed on your device with a key derived from your passphrase. A few older files may still have a readable name on our server until they are re-sealed.
s2.l3: Your vault passphrase. It is never sent to us.
s2.p2: Be honest with yourself about what this does not cover:
s2.l4: The web app is code that our servers send to your browser. If we, or someone who broke into our hosting, shipped a malicious update, it could capture your passphrase. The desktop and Android apps bundle their code, which narrows that risk but does not remove it.
s2.l5: We can see metadata: sizes, chunk counts, timestamps, folder structure, who you share with, and when you are active.
s2.l6: Your wrapped encryption keys are stored on our server. Someone who obtained them could try to guess a weak passphrase offline. Use a long, unique one.
s2.l7: Some features are deliberately not end-to-end private. The dead-man switch stores its contact email and message in plain text and our server emails them (see below). Text you put in a bug report or review is readable by us.

s3.p1: We keep what is needed to run the service.
s3.l1: Email address, username and a bcrypt hash of your password (never the password itself).
s3.l2: An optional display name and profile picture, stored as an inline image.
s3.l3: If you turn on two-factor sign-in: the authenticator secret and hashed backup codes. If you sign in with Google or GitHub: the provider's account ID.
s3.l4: Sessions: for each signed-in device, a hashed refresh token, a shortened IP address (the last part removed: /24 for IPv4, /48 for IPv6) and the browser's user agent. You can see these and sign devices out in Settings.
s3.l5: Per file: encrypted size, chunk count, timestamps, which folder it is in, the sealed name and the wrapped key that unlocks it. Per chunk: where the encrypted piece is stored.
s3.l6: Spaces: who is a member and their role. Share links: view counts, expiry and an optional bcrypt-hashed password.
s3.l7: Connections to storage platforms (see the next section).
s3.l8: An audit log of account events (sign-ins, failed attempts, password and 2FA changes, exports, deletion requests) with the shortened IP and user agent. It is linked to your account; it does not store your email address.
s3.l9: The audit log is kept for up to 365 days, and it is kept even after you delete your account (it holds your user ID, not a name).
s3.h4: Things you choose to send us
s3.l10: Bug reports: your text, an optional screenshot, the app version, platform, the page you were on and your user agent.
s3.l11: Reviews and feedback: your text, rating and display name. A review is only shown publicly if you allow it and it is approved.
s3.l12: Dead-man switch, if you set one up: a contact's email and name, your message and a timeout. These are stored unencrypted and emailed to your contact by our server if you stop checking in.
s3.l13: We do not run advertising or marketing trackers. We do not use Google Analytics, Sentry, PostHog or similar tools. The website uses Vercel Web Analytics for aggregate page-view statistics.

s4.p1: File contents are stored as encrypted chunks. Where they go depends on you:
s4.l1: Your own accounts. If you connect GitHub, GitLab, Hugging Face or Telegram, your chunks are stored there, under your account. You can reach them with those platforms' own tools, and their policies apply to what they hold.
s4.l2: Shared zcrypt storage. If you have not connected your own, your chunks go into storage accounts operated by zcrypt, with a 1 GiB limit per user. Anonymous Send, Pad and Transfer also use zcrypt-operated storage.
s4.p2: To upload and download for you, our server keeps your platform access tokens, encrypted at rest with a key derived from a server master key. That means our server can decrypt those tokens and use them to reach your storage accounts. It does so only to carry out your uploads, downloads and deletions. What it can reach there is still encrypted. Revoke a token at the platform at any time.

s5.p1: These services process data on our behalf. We list only the ones that exist today.
s5.l1: Neon: our PostgreSQL database (AWS, us-east-1). Holds everything in the sections above, but no file contents.
s5.l2: Vercel: hosts the website and web app, and provides Web Analytics.
s5.l3: Our backend server, reached through Cloudflare. Cloudflare sees traffic to our API and tells us your country, which we use only to suggest a language and do not store. The server host may change over time.
s5.l4: Resend: sends our emails: verification, magic sign-in links, password resets, new-device notices, account deletion notices and dead-man switch messages. They see the recipient address and message.
s5.l5: Google and GitHub, only if you choose to sign in with them.
s5.l6: GitHub, GitLab, Hugging Face and Telegram, as storage platforms (above).
s5.p1b: These providers may process data outside your country, mostly in the United States.
s5.p2: We do not sell your data. If we were legally compelled to disclose something, we could only hand over what we hold: the account data and metadata described here, never your file contents or names.

s6.p1: These tools work without an account.
s6.l1: Send. The file is encrypted in your browser and the key stays in the link you share. The encrypted file is stored on zcrypt-operated storage for up to 24 hours, then deleted, or deleted after it is downloaded if you chose burn after read. The limit is 50 MB per file. Anonymous senders are limited to 500 MB per rolling 24 hours, counted by shortened IP address, which we store to count it. The file name is stored by us as sent (sealed if your browser sealed it).
s6.l2: Pad. Encrypted text notes with an expiry or burn after read. The server stores ciphertext and the shortened IP of the creator.
s6.l3: Transfer. A device-to-device relay. The key is not sent to the relay.

s7.t: Cookies and storage on your device
s7.p1: We use no advertising cookies and show no cookie banner because we set none for tracking.
s7.l1: Sign-in cookie. An httpOnly cookie carries your refresh token so you stay signed in. The web app does not keep your access token in localStorage.
s7.l2: Preferences in localStorage: language, theme, view settings, a random device ID, and flags such as dismissed notices and what's-new seen. A minimal cached user record (ID, role, username) helps the app load.
s7.l3: Your passphrase. By default it is kept in memory only and forgotten after 15 minutes or when you lock the vault. If you tick "keep me unlocked on this device" (off by default), it is stored on this device, encrypted with a key kept in the same browser profile, so anyone with access to that profile can unlock your vault. The desktop app uses the operating system keychain instead.
s7.l4: The app may also cache file lists and thumbnails in your browser to load faster.

s8.l1: Account data is kept while your account exists.
s8.l2: Deleting your account (Settings) signs out all devices and starts a 7-day grace period; you can cancel it during that time. After that your account data is erased and your stored chunks are queued for deletion from the storage platforms, which can take time and can fail if a platform is unreachable or the token no longer works.
s8.l3: Audit log entries are kept up to 365 days, including after deletion. Backups of our database may hold older copies, and we have not set a fixed period for them. Bug reports you sent stay, without a link to your account.
s8.l4: Expired Send transfers and download tickets are cleaned up automatically (Send by 24 hours, with usage counters kept 48 hours).
s8.l5: Deleting a file moves it to trash; purging it queues its chunks for removal from the platform.

s9.p1: Whatever country you live in, you can:
s9.l1: Export your account data as a JSON file from Settings (file contents download separately, as ever).
s9.l5: Ask us by email about anything else: access, correction, restriction, objection, or a complaint. If you are in the EU or UK you can also complain to your data protection authority.
s9.p2: We process your data to provide the service you asked for (account, storage, sharing), to keep it secure and prevent abuse, and, for emails you request, to deliver them.

s10.p1: zcrypt is not meant for anyone under 16, and we do not knowingly collect data from children. Tell us and we will delete it.

s11.p1: If we change this policy we will update the date at the top. For significant changes we will email account holders or show a notice in the app. The full history is in the project's public git repository.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.lead: The rules, in plain language. Last updated October 11, 2026.

s1.p1: zcrypt is a free service run by one individual, Muhammad Wasif Malik, not a company. "We" means him. By creating an account or using zcrypt you agree to these Terms and to our <l1>Privacy Policy</l1>.

s2.l1: Give accurate details, and keep your password and vault passphrase safe. You are responsible for what happens under your account.
s2.l3: One person, one account. Do not sell or share access.

s3.p1: zcrypt encrypts your files on your device and stores the encrypted pieces. It is free, and it comes with limits that can change: storage on zcrypt-operated shared storage is capped (currently 1 GiB per user), a single file is capped, plans set how many uploads run at once, and anonymous Send is limited to 50 MB per file and 500 MB per day.
s3.p2: Connecting your own storage accounts (GitHub, GitLab, Hugging Face, Telegram) removes the shared cap. You are then bound by those platforms' own terms and limits, and you are responsible for their costs.
s3.p3: This is a one-person project. We may change, limit or discontinue features, and we make no promise of uptime.

s4.t: What you can and cannot do
s4.p1: You may not use zcrypt to:
s4.l1: store, share or distribute illegal content, or content that exploits or endangers children;
s4.l2: attack, probe or overload the service, or get around its limits, quotas or rate limits;
s4.l3: use zcrypt's shared storage as a free dumping ground, or create accounts or uploads in bulk by automation;
s4.l4: harass people or spread malware through shares, Send links or Spaces.
s4.p2: We cannot see your encrypted content, but we can see account activity and metadata, and we may act on it. Report abuse to the contact address below.

s5.p1: You keep all rights to your files. You give us only the permission needed to store and transmit them as you direct. zcrypt's source code is open; the zcrypt name and logo are ours.
s5.p2: We cannot read, recover or reset your vault passphrase. If you lose it, your files are gone for good, and nobody, including us, can get them back. Use a password manager.
s5.p3: Platforms like GitHub, GitLab, Hugging Face or Telegram can delete, restrict or lose data, or suspend your account, for their own reasons. We cannot prevent that or recover what they lose. Keep another copy of anything that matters.

s6.p1: You can delete your account at any time in Settings; see the Privacy Policy for what happens next. We may suspend or end accounts that break these Terms or put the service or other people at risk. We will tell you why when we can.

s7.t: No warranty, and limits on liability
s7.p1: zcrypt is provided "as is" and "as available", with no warranties. As far as the law allows, we are not responsible for lost data (including from a forgotten passphrase, platform outage, platform suspension, bug or shutdown) or for indirect or consequential losses. Because the service is free, any liability we do have is limited to the amount you paid us, which is zero. Some places do not allow some of these limits, and those limits apply only as far as the law lets them.

s8.p1: We may change these Terms. We will update the date above and, for significant changes, email you or show a notice in the app. If you keep using zcrypt after a change takes effect, you accept it.
